celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿تَبَارَكَ﴾ exalted above the attributes of created beings is ﴿الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ﴾ in His disposal ﴿الْمُلْكُ﴾ the authority and the power, ﴿وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَ الْمَوْتَ﴾ in this world ﴿وَالْحَيَاةَ﴾ in the Hereafter; or both are in this world: the sperm-drop has life come upon it, and it (life) is that by which there is sensation, while death is its opposite or its absence — two views — and creating, on the second (view), is in the sense of decreeing; ﴿لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ﴾ to test you in life, ﴿أَيُّكُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا﴾ most obedient to Allah. ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ﴾ in His vengeance on whoever disobeys Him, ﴿الْغَفُورُ﴾ to whoever repents to Him.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ طِبَاقًا﴾ one above another, without touching. ﴿مَا تَرَى فِي خَلْقِ الرَّحْمَنِ﴾ for them or for others ﴿مِنْ تَفَاوُتٍ﴾ disparity and lack of proportion. ﴿فَارْجِعِ الْبَصَرَ﴾ turn it back to the sky: ﴿هَلْ تَرَى﴾ in it ﴿مِنْ فُطُورٍ﴾ cracks and fissures?

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿ثُمَّ ارْجِعِ الْبَصَرَ كَرَّتَيْنِ﴾ time after time; ﴿يَنْقَلِبْ﴾ will return ﴿إِلَيْكَ الْبَصَرُ خَاسِئًا﴾ humbled, for not perceiving any flaw, ﴿وَهُوَ حَسِيرٌ﴾ cut off from seeing a flaw.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ زَيَّنَّا السَّمَاءَ الدُّنْيَا﴾ the nearest to the earth ﴿بِمَصَابِيحَ﴾ with stars, ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاهَا رُجُومًا﴾ missiles ﴿لِلشَّيَاطِينِ﴾ when they eavesdrop, in that a shooting flame detaches from the star like a firebrand taken from a fire and kills the jinni or deranges him — not that the star moves from its place; ﴿وَأَعْتَدْنَا لَهُمْ عَذَابَ السَّعِيرِ﴾ the kindled fire.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَلِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ is it.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿إِذَا أُلْقُوا فِيهَا سَمِعُوا لَهَا شَهِيقًا﴾ a hideous sound like the sound of a donkey, ﴿وَهِيَ تَفُورُ﴾ boiling.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿تَكَادُ تَمَيَّزُ﴾ — and it has been read [تَتَمَيَّزُ], according to the original form — burst apart ﴿مِنَ الْغَيْظِ﴾ in anger at the disbelievers. ﴿كُلَّمَا أُلْقِيَ فِيهَا فَوْجٌ﴾ a group of them, ﴿سَأَلَهُمْ خَزَنَتُهَا﴾ a question of rebuke: ﴿أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ نَذِيرٌ﴾ a messenger warning you of the punishment of Allah the Exalted?

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿قَالُوا بَلَى قَدْ جَاءَنَا نَذِيرٌ فَكَذَّبْنَا وَقُلْنَا مَا نَزَّلَ اللَّهُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِنْ﴾ not ﴿أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا فِي ضَلَالٍ كَبِيرٍ﴾: it may be part of the speech of the angels to the disbelievers when they reported the denial, or part of the speech of the disbelievers to the warners.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا لَوْ كُنَّا نَسْمَعُ﴾, i.e. a hearing of understanding, ﴿أَوْ نَعْقِلُ﴾, i.e. a reasoning of reflection, ﴿مَا كُنَّا فِي أَصْحَابِ السَّعِيرِ﴾

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿فَاعْتَرَفُوا﴾, where confession does not benefit, ﴿بِذَنْبِهِمْ﴾ — and it is denying the warners. ﴿فَسُحْقًا﴾, with sukūn on the ḥāʾ and with ḍamma, ﴿لِأَصْحَابِ السَّعِيرِ﴾: so far be they from the mercy of Allah!

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ﴾ fear Him ﴿بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ in their absence from people's eyes, and so obey Him in secret, so in public all the more, ﴿لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ كَبِيرٌ﴾, i.e. Paradise.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَأَسِرُّوا﴾, O people, ﴿قَوْلَكُمْ أَوِ اجْهَرُوا بِهِ إِنَّهُ﴾ the Exalted ﴿عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ﴾ of what is in them, so how (much more) of what you utter! The occasion of the revelation of that is that the idolaters said to one another, "Keep your speech secret, so that the God of Muhammad does not hear you."

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿أَلَا يَعْلَمُ مَنْ خَلَقَ﴾ what you keep secret? I.e. is His knowledge of that absent? ﴿وَهُوَ اللَّطِيفُ﴾ in His knowledge, ﴿الْخَبِيرُ﴾ in it. No!

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ ذَلُولًا﴾ easy to walk upon, ﴿فَامْشُوا فِي مَنَاكِبِهَا﴾ its sides, ﴿وَكُلُوا مِنْ رِزْقِهِ﴾ created for your sake; ﴿وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ﴾ from the graves, for the recompense.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿أَأَمِنْتُمْ﴾ — with both hamzas pronounced fully, with the second eased, with an alif inserted between it and the other and without it, and with it changed into an alif — ﴿مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ﴾ His authority and His power, ﴿أَنْ يَخْسِفَ﴾ — a badal (substitute) from مَنْ — ﴿بِكُمُ الْأَرْضَ فَإِذَا هِيَ تَمُورُ﴾ moves with you and rises above you?

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿أَمْ أَمِنْتُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ أَنْ يُرْسِلَ﴾ — a badal (substitute) from مَنْ — ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ حَاصِبًا﴾ a wind pelting you with pebbles? ﴿فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ﴾ on seeing the punishment ﴿كَيْفَ نَذِيرِ﴾ My warning of punishment, i.e. that it is true.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ of the nations; ﴿فَكَيْفَ كَانَ نَكِيرِ﴾ My disapproval of them for the denial when destroying them, i.e. that it is true.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا﴾ look ﴿إِلَى الطَّيْرِ فَوْقَهُمْ﴾ in the air ﴿صَافَّاتٍ﴾ spreading their wings ﴿وَيَقْبِضْنَ﴾ their wings after spreading, i.e. and folding? ﴿مَا يُمْسِكُهُنَّ﴾ from falling, in the state of spreading and folding, ﴿إِلَّا الرَّحْمَنُ﴾ by His power. ﴿إِنَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ بَصِيرٌ﴾. The meaning is: have they not inferred from the birds staying firm in the air Our power to do to them what preceded, and other punishment?

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿أَمَّنْ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿هَذَا﴾: its khabar (predicate); ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a badal (substitute) from هَذَا; ﴿هُوَ جُنْدٌ﴾ helpers ﴿لَكُمْ﴾: the ṣila (relative clause) of الَّذِي; ﴿يَنْصُرُكُمْ﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of جُنْدٌ; ﴿مِنْ دُونِ الرَّحْمَنِ﴾, i.e. other than Him, warding off His punishment from you? I.e. you have no helper. ﴿إِنِ﴾ not ﴿الْكَافِرُونَ إِلَّا فِي غُرُورٍ﴾: Satan deluded them that the punishment would not descend on them.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿أَمَّنْ هَذَا الَّذِي يَرْزُقُكُمْ إِنْ أَمْسَكَ﴾ the Most Merciful ﴿رِزْقَهُ﴾, i.e. the rain, from you? The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. then who will provide for you? I.e. you have no provider other than Him. ﴿بَلْ لَجُّوا﴾ they have persisted ﴿فِي عُتُوٍّ﴾ arrogance ﴿وَنُفُورٍ﴾ distancing from the truth.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿أَفَمَنْ يَمْشِي مُكِبًّا﴾ fallen ﴿عَلَى وَجْهِهِ أَهْدَى أَمَّنْ يَمْشِي سَوِيًّا﴾ upright ﴿عَلَى صِرَاطٍ﴾ a path ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾? The khabar (predicate) of the second مَنْ is omitted, indicated by the khabar of the first, i.e. أَهْدَى (better guided). The likeness concerns the believer and the disbeliever, i.e. which of the two is upon guidance?

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ الَّذِي أَنْشَأَكُمْ﴾ created you ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ السَّمْعَ وَالْأَبْصَارَ وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ﴾ the hearts; ﴿قَلِيلًا مَا تَشْكُرُونَ﴾: مَا is added (mazīda), and the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnifa), informing of the very great paucity of their gratitude for these blessings.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ الَّذِي ذَرَأَكُمْ﴾ created you ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ وَإِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ﴾ for the reckoning.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾ to the believers: ﴿مَتَى هَذَا الْوَعْدُ﴾ the promise of the gathering, ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ in it?

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَا الْعِلْمُ﴾ of its coming ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَإِنَّمَا أَنَا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ clear in warning.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ﴾, i.e. the punishment, after the gathering, ﴿زُلْفَةً﴾ near, ﴿سِيئَتْ﴾ were blackened ﴿وُجُوهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَقِيلَ﴾, i.e. the keepers said to them: ﴿هَذَا﴾, i.e. the punishment, ﴿الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ﴾ — about the warning of it — ﴿تَدَّعُونَ﴾ that you would not be resurrected. This is the narration of a state to come, expressed in the past form because of the certainty of its occurrence.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَهْلَكَنِيَ اللَّهُ وَمَنْ مَعِيَ﴾ of the believers, with His punishment, as you intend, ﴿أَوْ رَحِمَنَا﴾ and did not punish us, ﴿فَمَنْ يُجِيرُ الْكَافِرِينَ مِنْ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾? I.e. they have no protector from it.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ الرَّحْمَنُ آمَنَّا بِهِ وَعَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْنَا فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ﴾, with tāʾ and with yāʾ, on seeing the punishment, ﴿مَنْ هُوَ فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ clear: is it we, or you, or they?

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَصْبَحَ مَاؤُكُمْ غَوْرًا﴾ sunk into the earth, ﴿فَمَنْ يَأْتِيكُمْ بِمَاءٍ مَعِينٍ﴾ flowing, which hands and buckets can reach, like your water? I.e. none brings it but Allah the Exalted; so how do you deny that He will resurrect you? It is recommended that the reciter say after مَعِينٍ, "Allah, Lord of the worlds", as has come in the ḥadīth. This verse was recited in the presence of one of the tyrants, and he said, "Axes and pickaxes will bring it"; so the water of his eyes went and he became blind. We seek refuge in Allah from audacity against Allah and against His signs.
